head: Free phone upgrade scam: the caller asks you to send the new phone back
dek: Scammers call claiming to be your mobile network and offer a free upgrade. A real phone arrives, then a second call says it was sent by mistake, and a courier takes it to the scammers while you keep paying the contract.
details: Malwarebytes says the call usually comes from a spoofed number, and the return label points to an address the criminals chose instead of the network's returns center. Nearly 30,000 cases were reported in the UK last year.
where: UK and other countries, by phone
means: An unexpected call offering a free upgrade, followed by a request to return the phone, is the pattern to watch for.
todo: Upgrade only by calling your network yourself or in its store; if you already sent a phone back, call your provider on its official number and ask for a fraud investigation.
